findings: Frequency-controlled g8 reduced mean prediction disagreements only modestly, from 586.67 to 558.67.
Frequency-controlled g8 did not reduce mean absolute logit error: it increased from 0.4558 for standard g8 to 0.4879.
Mean maximum absolute logit error per sample increased from 1.6193 to 1.7083.
Mean reference accuracy fell from 0.83647 for standard g8 to 0.82753 for repeated-low-frequency g8.
Mean Q.ANT accuracy fell from 0.82103 to 0.81417.
The g4 baseline remained the only Pareto point in this experiment at 62,730 parameters and mean Q.ANT accuracy 0.82987.
interpretation: Removing frequencies 5-8 while holding the eight-component parameter count fixed did not solve the model-level reference-to-Q.ANT mismatch. Exp014 established that single-operation residual grows with frequency, but Exp018 shows that this fact alone is insufficient to explain the larger g8 deployment error. A more plausible next target is error accumulation across the weighted sum of Fourier components, including the scale and distribution of learned amplitudes.
next_research_direction: Directly measure how learned amplitude magnitude and component-wise Q.ANT residual contributions accumulate into output-logit error for locked g4 and g8 models, then use those measurements to design a targeted regularization or normalization intervention.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Three seeds and three epochs limit precision.
Repeating frequencies 1-4 preserves parameter count but changes the representational function class relative to distinct frequencies 1-8.
The experiment does not isolate amplitude scale or cancellation between signed component errors.
